topic: Country with the most bird species: Colombia, about 1,969 species on the national checklist of the Colombian Committee of Ornithological Records (roughly a fifth of the world's ~11,000 species), ahead of Peru (~1,890), Brazil (~1,860) and Indonesia (~1,700+). The diversity is driven by the three Andean cordilleras and their isolated valleys, plus Caribbean and Pacific coasts, Amazon and Orinoco lowlands. Colombia has the most hummingbird species of any country (over 160) and new species continue to be described; the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta has one of the world's highest concentrations of endemic birds.
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: Brazil, with most of the Amazon, must have the most bird species.
myths.reality: Brazil ranks third behind Colombia and Peru; Colombia's Andean valleys and two coasts pack more species into an eighth of Brazil's area.
